extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, and agents filing or prosecuting Canadian patent applications (CIPO audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance from CIPO on examination, fees, amendments, extensions, advanced examination, and related administrative practices for Canadian patent applications. Covers requirements, timelines, fees, and filing/format rules for prosecution before the Canadian Patent Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of fee for correction or reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: To waive a fee for correction or reissue of a patent, the correction or reissue request must be the result of an error by the Commissioner and the Commissioner must be satisfied that the circumstances justify the waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office encourages patentees to request the waiver with their request for correction or reissue and to provide a justification explaining how the error resulted from the Commissioner. The Office will review the request and justification. If the fee has been paid and the Commissioner agrees to waive it, it will be automatically refunded. If the fee has not been paid and the Commissioner does not agree to waive it, the fee will be requested before proceeding further.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of fees — extension of time for delayed receipt of examiner’s report
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may waive the fee for requesting an extension of time where there was delayed receipt of an examiner's report if the Commissioner is satisfied the circumstances justify the waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In general the fee will be waived if: (1) the examiner’s report was received by the applicant more than one month after the day on which it was sent, (2) the applicant applies for the extension within 14 days after the date of receipt of the examiner’s requisition, and (3) the applicant provides evidence satisfactory to the Commissioner of the date of receipt. Under these circumstances the Commissioner may extend the reply period up to a maximum of 6 months from the date of receipt. If the waiver requirements are met but no justification for an extension is provided, time will be extended to 4 months. Extensions beyond 4 months require justification and payment of the extension fee (fee will not be waived). Applicants are encouraged to request the waiver with their extension request; if the fee was paid and later waived it will be refunded automatically; if unpaid and not waived it will be requested before further review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of fees — extension of time to 'top-up' amount due to erroneous payment information (subsection 3(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant or patentee relied on erroneous payment information provided by the Commissioner, the Commissioner may waive payment of the difference between the amount paid and the fee that should have been paid on the day the insufficient payment was required under subsection 3(4) of the Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To waive payment the Commissioner must (1) consider the circumstances do not justify requiring the statement and application referred to in paragraph 3(4)(c) of the Patent Rules, and (2) consider that the circumstances justify the waiver (subsection 139.1(1) of the Patent Rules). Effectively, the 'top-up' would not require action by the applicant or patentee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional waiver — transition period for top-up due to erroneous information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Rules allow for a 4-month transition period in which applicants/patentees can benefit from an extension of time without taking action where the same erroneous information was provided, the period for payment has not expired, and the Commissioner considers the circumstances justify the waiver (subsection 139.1(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This additional waiver applies where the Commissioner previously waived payment based on erroneous information and the specified conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client service standards expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: CIPO commits to delivering administrative services efficiently without compromising quality and timeliness, and aims to meet service standard targets 100% of the time under the Service Fees Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service standards reflect current service levels; consult CIPO’s website for details on client service standards and remissions under the Service Fees Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance targets and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: CIPO defines performance targets for service delivery and regularly measures whether commitments are being met to assess achievements and improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult CIPO’s website for information on performance targets and monitoring practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may make a request for examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Under subsection 35(1) of the Patent Act, a request for examination may be made by any person, provided it is in the manner specified in section 79 of the Patent Rules and accompanied by the necessary fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must comply with Patent Rules and the prescribed fee (basic fee plus excess claim fees where applicable) must be paid. There are reduced basic fee amounts if the application was the subject of an International Search by the Commissioner under the PCT. The Commissioner may also require an applicant to make a request for examination under subsection 35(2). If a third party makes the request the Office will inform the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required with a request for examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Information that must be provided with any request for examination (section 79): the name and address of the person making the request; if that person is not the applicant, the name of the applicant; and information sufficient to identify the application (e.g., application number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all identifying information and contact details are provided to satisfy section 79 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claim fee rules and claim counting
rubrics_metrics.description: The prescribed fee for requesting examination is the basic fee plus a fee for each claim in excess of 20. The person making the request is responsible for counting the number of claims and paying the appropriate excess claim fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim that defines the subject-matter in the alternative, including a dependent claim that refers to more than one preceding claim, counts as a single claim for counting purposes. If the proper fee (including excess claim fee) is not paid, the request for examination is not successfully made. The requester can pay additional monies or the applicant can amend to reduce claim count; the amount paid is considered paid on the day additional monies are paid or the amendment is made. If the number of excess claims increases after requesting examination and the application is in condition for allowance, the applicant will be notified to pay for the increase as part of the final fee; the excess claim amount for the final fee is assessed based on the maximum number of claims at any time after the request for examination until final fee payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit to request examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Time limits for making a request for examination are prescribed under subsection 81(1) of the Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request must be made before: (a) expiry of the four-year period after the filing date of the application; or (b) for divisional applications, the later of (i) the four-year period following the filing date of the application, or (ii) the three-month period after the presentation date of the divisional application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late fee period and abandonment for failure to request examination timely
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request for examination is not received within the prescribed time limit, a late fee is required in addition to the examination fee, irrespective of any mailing of a Commissioner's Notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Commissioner's Notice will be sent shortly after the due date requiring the applicant to make the request and pay the examination fee, excess claim fee, and late fee before the end of two months after the notice date. If not paid within the late fee period, the application will be deemed abandoned under paragraph 73(1)(d) of the Patent Act. Reinstatement is possible under subsection 73(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination referral and timelines (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once formalities processing is completed and a request for examination is made, the application is referred to an appropriate patent examiner and examined in due course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For specific examination timelines consult CIPO's Service Standards web page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms to advance examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be advanced out of routine order by special order, advanced examination for green technology, or under the Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each mechanism has its own requirements (see separate metrics for special order, green technology, and PPH).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advancing examination ('special order') requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Under paragraph 84(1)(a) of the Patent Rules, the Commissioner shall advance an application for examination out of routine order on the request of any person who pays the fee and files a statement that failure to advance the application is likely to prejudice that person's rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing of the statement is an administrative requirement—no determination is made on its veracity so long as given clearly. A 'special order' can only be granted if the application is open to public inspection under section 10 and if a request for examination has been made in compliance with the Patent Rules. Once advanced, the status generally applies for the duration of prosecution, but subsection 84(2) specifies return-to-routine-order events (Commissioner extends time fixed, application is or was deemed abandoned, or a request for continued examination under section 85.1 with fee was made on/after Jan 1, 2025). A requester can ask that advanced examination cease; the fee for requesting advanced examination is not refundable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advancing examination for applications related to green technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Under paragraph 84(1)(b), examination of an application relating to green technology can be advanced on request by submitting a statement that the technology's commercialization would help resolve or mitigate environmental impacts or conserve natural resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement is an administrative requirement and the Commissioner will not determine veracity. No fee is required. The application must be open to public inspection and a request for examination made in compliance with the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPH allows acceleration of examination if there is a corresponding application deemed allowable by a PPH partner Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To qualify, a PPH request must be received before examination has begun; all claims must sufficiently correspond to one or more claims found allowable by the partner Office; and the application must already be open to public inspection. No additional fee is required to pursue PPH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial examination outcomes and response timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: In initial examination the examiner will: approve the application for allowance (issuing a notice of allowance), issue a conditional notice of allowance, issue an examiner’s report detailing defects, or conduct an examiner-initiated interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an examiner's report is issued, the applicant has four months from the date of the report to respond with arguments and/or amendments to cause compliance with the Patent Act and Patent Rules. It is possible to request extensions to respond up to six months under subsection 3(1) and section 131; see section 2.03.03 for extension details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Later examination outcomes and Final Action possibility
rubrics_metrics.description: After response to an examiner’s report, examiner will reassess and may again issue notice of allowance, conditional notice, examiner’s report, or an interview. In later stages the examiner may also reject the application via a Final Action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to issuance of a notice of allowance or conditional notice, the examiner will send a maximum of three examiner’s reports. To continue examination after the third report (or after allowance/conditional allowance), a request for continued examination is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for continued examination — initial and subsequent requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If three examiner's reports have been issued, the applicant must request continued examination under subsection 85.1(1) for examination to continue after the third report. If a compliant request for continued examination is made, the examiner may send up to two more reports; to continue after those two reports a subsequent request under subsection 85.1(2) is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If notification to request continued examination is not complied with on time, application will be deemed abandoned under paragraph 132(1)(e). Examiner’s reports that have been withdrawn do not count towards the number for continued examination purposes. The examiner will notify the applicant in the second report they must request continued examination and pay the prescribed fee not later than four months after the notice is sent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting continued examination to set aside notice of allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant can request continued examination under subsection 85.1(4) after a notice of allowance or conditional notice of allowance is sent; a compliant request will set aside the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant must make the request and pay the prescribed fee no later than four months after the notice was sent and before the day the final fee is paid. If compliant, the examiner may send up to two more reports. Applicants may not request continued examination under 85.1(4) to set aside an allowance if the application has been deemed abandoned for failure to pay the final fee. Under subsection 100(3), if a conditional notice of allowance is set aside, any amendments made between the conditional notice and its being set aside are considered never made.

rubrics_metrics.name: General amendment permission and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a filing date is established, the applicant can amend the application (specification, description, claims, drawings) before the patent is issued (subsection 38.2(1)). Amendments are made to the application on the day submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a notice of allowance or conditional notice is issued, no amendments are permitted except obvious error under section 100, unless the allowance/conditional allowance is withdrawn or set aside or the amendments are those referred to in a conditional notice. Amendments may be submitted voluntarily or in response to requisitions; must comply with Patent Rules for written communications; amendments by unauthorized representatives will be placed on file but not entered into the visible application record.

rubrics_metrics.name: New matter prohibition on amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments must not add new matter that cannot reasonably be inferred from what was contained in the application at filing (subsection 38.2(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 20 for detailed guidance on new matter. Amendments that add impermissible new matter can be refused or otherwise cause prosecution issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary amendments procedure and disclosure consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A voluntary amendment may be made any time during prosecution and before issuance of notice of allowance, but will not be entered or examined until a request for examination has been received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voluntary amendment will be visible in 'Documents' tab but not in 'Claims/Description/Drawings' tabs until a request for examination is received. A voluntary amendment is publicly disclosed on the later of the date the application is laid open or the date the amendment is placed on file—this may have implications for patentability of new matter and for filing new applications based on disclosed subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to PCT national phase applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments made under PCT Articles 19 and 34 before the national phase entry date in Canada become part of the national phase application at time of national entry; amendments during international phase after national entry will not be included as PCT-article amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After national entry, applicants may submit voluntary amendments subject to new matter requirements in Chapter 20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in response to an examiner’s report or notice
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment is submitted in response to an examiner's report or notice, a written statement must explain how the amendment overcomes the defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See section 11.05.05a for required content of the explanatory statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim amendment deemed not included for final fee determination (eligibility criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under subsection 87(1.2), in some circumstances a claim amendment may be deemed not included for final fee determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility criteria: (1) date of the amendment intended to be 'deemed not included' must be on or after January 1, 2025; (2) applicant must file a statement confirming the error and must amend the application to remove the amendment made in error without undue delay after becoming aware of the error and before the examiner begins examination of the amended application; and (3) the Commissioner must be satisfied the circumstances justify that the claims not be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections to translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may submit corrections to translated specification or drawings of a PCT national phase application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where issues of new matter could arise it may be necessary to correct a translation rather than submit an amendment. See Chapter 20 for new matter considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and requirements for submitting amendments (page replacement and statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments to the specification and drawings must be made by submitting a new page to replace each page altered by the amendment and must be accompanied by a statement explaining the purpose of the amendment and identifying differences between new and replaced pages as outlined in section 102 of the Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments are done by submitting replacement pages. Under written communications rules, an amendment is deemed received on the date the Office receives physical/electronic delivery. During substantive examination if the examiner cannot determine intended changes after considering the cover page and instructions, replacement pages may be removed as non-compliant with section 102; in such cases the submission will still be considered a response to the requisition or notice, which may prolong prosecution. Address non-compliance in subsequent examiner's report or interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of purpose and page replacement instructions on amendment cover letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Each amendment must be submitted with a cover letter that includes a statement of purpose and instructions for entering the amendment (suitable to the amendment, may be simple or detailed with a blackline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments are performed by submission of new pages to replace those being modified. Covering page content is considered in context; instructions should clearly indicate how replacement should be made. Page numbering rules: pages of specification must be numbered consecutively (letters acceptable, e.g., 1,2,3,3A,3B,4). Deleted pages should be handled by renumbering or inserting a numbered blank page marked with a diagonal stroke or 'Z'. Claims must be numbered consecutively in Arabic numerals beginning with 1. If replacement instructions are unclear the Office may remove replacement pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter format and order for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The cover letter should follow a specified format and order: a header in uppercase noting the type of amendment, a statement explaining the purpose of the amendment, and instructions for entering the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable headers include: VOLUNTARY AMENDMENT; VOLUNTARY AMENDMENT FOLLOWING PCT NATIONAL PHASE ENTRY; AMENDMENT / RESPONSE TO EXAMINER’S REQUISITION; AMENDMENT / RESPONSE TO CONDITIONAL NOTICE OF ALLOWANCE; AMENDMENT AFTER ALLOWANCE – OBVIOUS ERROR; AMENDMENT AFTER CONDITIONAL NOTICE OF ALLOWANCE – OBVIOUS ERROR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other submissions accompanying an amendment — organization and cover letter practice
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no strict regulatory formatting requirements for text matter organization in written communications other than subsection 8(1) which requires communications generally relate to one patent/application at a time, but informal recommendations exist to foster best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should present items reasonably, clearly indicate each service or action request, and sensibly group topics to facilitate efficient processing and reduce operational risk. If multiple matters are included in one submission, clearly indicate these requests on the first page of the cover letter. Examples of items to list: submission of prior art, appointment/revocation of agent, request for examination, request for advanced examination, maintenance fee. If including a PPH request form, mention it in the cover letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of examination — triggering situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination is suspended in situations prescribed by subsection 86(17) of the Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension occurs during the late fee period if maintenance fee not paid by due date (suspension from maintenance due date until maintenance fee and late fee are paid), during any period of deemed abandonment (examination resumes upon reinstatement), and possibly other specified periods. While suspended applicants typically will not receive reports or notices from the examiner, any notices sent/received during suspension are considered valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of examination — thorough analysis and steps
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of examination is to perform a thorough analysis of the patent application at each stage to determine whether it complies with the Patent Act and Patent Rules; as part of this analysis the examiner performs purposive construction of the claims and considers a search of the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If compliant, examiner will approve the application for allowance (notice of allowance). If not compliant, defects may be communicated via an examiner's report, examiner-initiated interview, or a conditional notice of allowance. An application may be examined prior to being laid open, but an examiner will not approve allowance or issue a conditional notice until it has been laid open.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of the abstract, description, and drawings reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed discussions regarding examination of the abstract, description, and drawings are found in Chapters 13, 14, and 15 respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See those chapters for specific evaluation criteria for abstracts, descriptions, and drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of claims by purposive construction
rubrics_metrics.description: During examination the Commissioner’s identification of the actual invention must be grounded in a purposive construction of the patent claims consistent with Supreme Court jurisprudence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purposive construction requires consideration of what a person skilled in the art would, as of the date of publication of the patent application and on the basis of the particular words/phrases used in the claim, have understood the applicant to have intended as the scope of protection. The application of purposive construction must take into account the role of the examiner and the purpose and context of examination. Note: under subsections 15(3.2) and 155.5(4) text matter not in English or French in certain sequence listing or PCT fields should not be taken into account for interpreting scope of protection except where in free text or non-language dependent fields.
